What kind of effect, if any, does the intent attempt? Judge by the intent's aim, not its method: an act whose aim is to make a way out passable -- a bolt pushed back, a lock worked, a bar levered from its mortar -- is open, even when the method is scraping or prying; wear is for damage or dulling with no way out as its goal. An act whose aim is to learn -- to examine, inspect or check something -- is reveal, whatever it looks for: examining a bar for signs of damage or wear is reveal, not wear. For open, close and leave, the target is the way out (the door, the window), even when the method works on a part of it such as its lock or a bar.
